2001 Studio Album 14 Songs

Midnight Drivers

The 2001 Nocturnal Highway Album

The lost 1987 sophomore concept album. Rejected by Apex Records for its moody, atmospheric Darkwave tone, the master tapes sat in the vault for over a decade. Resurrected and released independently by Engine Room Records in 2001, this album finally bridges the gap between the vibrant city lights of Side A and the isolating sanctuary of Side B.

2003 Studio Album 10 Songs

Mile Marker 98

The 2003 "Twin Moons" Project (Moon 2)

The second half of the 2003 'Twin Moons' project. Acting as the 'Engine', this album features exclusively male vocals from Ryan O'Connell. Stripping away the celestial calm, it unleashes blistering, distorted electric guitars and aggressive rock energy. Released simultaneously with its twin, it explores the destructive side of gravity and serves as a heavy, visceral confrontation with the Crash of '90.

2003 Studio Album 10 Songs

Sanctuary (Zero-G)

The 2003 "Twin Moons" Project (Moon 1)

The first half of the 2003 'Twin Moons' project. Acting as the 'Anchor', this album features exclusively female vocals from Cassidy O'Connell. It is the ultimate showcase of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™—a mathematically precise, zero-gravity atmospheric masterpiece recorded while the band constructed their permanent Blacksburg studio. It represents finding a peaceful, silent sanctuary in the endless black.

2004 Studio Album 11 Songs

Progress Street

The 2004 Blacksburg Homecoming Album (Final Release Before the Burnout Hiatus)

A heartfelt, 1980s-inspired AOR and stadium synth-rock album from The Stardust Engine, recorded in 2004 at their home on Progress Street NE in Blacksburg, Virginia. Making the full-blooded 1980s melodic rock record that Apex Records never let them make in 1987, Progress Street celebrates collegiate roots, upright pianos, second-hand 1984 synthesizers, and unbreakable family unity—immortalized on the cover alongside the band's brand-new custom 2004 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 low-floor shuttle coach before exhaustion forced them into their Burnout Hiatus.

2011 Studio Album 14 Songs

Starfield Calibration

Celebrating 25 Years Since Ignition (The Forger's Call) Shook The Crucible (Oct 18, 1986 – Oct 18, 2011)

Released on Tuesday, October 18, 2011—at the midpoint of the band's Burnout Hiatus and on the exact 25th Anniversary of 'Ignition (The Forger's Call)' making its thunderous Saturday night debut inside The Crucible on October 18, 1986—Starfield Calibration reimagines fourteen foundational Stardust Engine classics (1987–2001) entirely within 'The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™' (a proprietary trademark of Michael P. Ragsdale / RaggieSoft Media / Engine Room Records™; '80s Cosmic Pop' is the open generic genre name free for everyone to use). Featuring driving 4/4 gated percussion, shimmering analog synthesizers, Evan Wright's melodic fretless basslines, and lush zero-gravity spatial reverb, this silver-anniversary hiatus release reminded Forger Nation that the family was still in orbit.

2015 Studio Album 11 Songs

Reignition

The 2015 Post-Hiatus Comeback Studio Album

Ten years after exhaustion led the family to step away from the road on 2004's Progress Street ('Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street'), The Stardust Engine returns rested, recharged, and ready to perform again. Released in October 2015 immediately following Holly O'Connell's August 2015 Delaware Migration, Reignition ends the decade-long Burnout Hiatus with eleven brand-new 1980s AOR and cosmic synth-rock anthems.

1999 Live Album 12 Songs

Hard Reset Live

The 1998–1999 Freedom Era World Tour

Recorded during the 1998–1999 Hard Reset World Tour—the band's first headlining tour since the 1990 Des Moines bus crash and their 1992 emancipation from Apex Records. Opening with the three-part 'Stardust Suite' ('The Stardust Engine', 'Hard Reset', and 'Brand New Scene') and closing with 'Electric Color', this live album permanently retires the traumatic Apex ballad 'If You Walked Away' in favor of 'Echoes in the Wire'.

2002 Live Album 14 Songs

Live at the Chancellery

The 2001–2002 Across The World Tour — Charlottesville Arena Encore Introducing Crimson Node

Recorded in May 2002 at The Chancellery in Charlottesville, Virginia during the 2001–2002 Across The World Tour and released in October 2002 following the debut of Crimson Node. Opens with 'The Stardust Engine', closes the main set with 'Electric Color', and culminates in the historic surprise encore where Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell officially introduce Crimson Node to the world with a joint performance of 'The Flight Path'.

2003 Live Album 14 Songs

Live in Virginia Beach

Recorded Live at CTI Virginia Beach Amphitheater • First Recorded Live Album Performance of "The Flight Path" (Mid-Concert Placement)

Recorded at the CTI Virginia Beach Amphitheater in Virginia Beach, Virginia on the 2001–2002 Midnight Drivers / Across The World Tour and released in February 2003 following Crimson Node and Live at the Chancellery. Having road-tested a mysterious unnamed new song for a few weeks on tour, The Stardust Engine tests whether the 20,000-strong hometown Virginia Beach crowd knows the words mid-concert—marking the first time 'The Flight Path' was ever recorded for a future live album while fans still believed it was simply a new Stardust Engine track.

2005 Live Album 14 Songs

Live in Norfolk

The 2003–2004 Twin Moons & Progress Street Tour Finale at the Norfolk Prism Arena

Recorded under the concrete dome of the Norfolk Prism Arena at the culmination of the grueling 2003–2004 Twin Moons & Progress Street Tour. Opening with 'The Stardust Engine' and closing with 'Electric Color', this triumphant yet exhausting coastal Virginia performance marks the final live concert before the family turned off the switches and entered their decade-long Burnout Hiatus (2005–2014).

2016 Live Album 34 Songs

Live at the Crucible

3-Disc Live Box Set • Recorded Live Inside The Crucible (May 21, 2016) • Released Homecoming Weekend at the CPI Campus Bookstore (October 15, 2016)

The band's most important live album. Recorded live on Saturday, May 21, 2016 inside The Crucible in Blacksburg, Virginia—Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute's 65,000-seat stadium and the loudest house in all of college football—and released commercially during CPI Homecoming Weekend on October 15, 2016. With no opening act, CPI Alumni (Class of 1989) return home for a seven-act, 34-track career-spanning stadium show marking the final concert of a touring The Stardust Engine before launching their annual Forger Nation Summer Festival residency in Blacksburg in August 2017. Opens with the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers ('Ignition: The Forger's Call', 'CPI Tech Triumph', and 'The Stardust Engine'), includes the ONLY recorded live performance of Cassidy's 13-minute magnum opus 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' anchoring the 10-song Twin Moons cosmic journey (Act III: Cosmic Tidal Lock + Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98), an intimate four-song acoustic block pairing Our Own Frequency with a stripped-down piano-and-acoustic-guitar rendition of 'Still Your Safe Person', the live concert debut of 'Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible', a hometown singalong on 'Neon on the Huckleberry Trail', a false ending on 'Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street', and the secret 5:26 1980s Stadium Rock (AOR) closing reclamation of 'Electric Color'.

2016 Compilation 16 Songs

The Forger's Call

30th-Anniversary CPI & Blacksburg Archival Compilation (1986–2016) • Companion Anthology to Live at the Crucible

Released on CPI Homecoming Weekend (October 15, 2016) alongside Live at the Crucible—both as a companion anthology inside the Live at the Crucible 30th-Anniversary Box Set at the CPI Campus Bookstore and as a standalone archival compilation—The Forger's Call spans thirty years (1986–2016) of previously uncollected Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) and Blacksburg vault recordings. Anchored at Track 1 by the official October 1986 Crucible Stadium Master of 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' (played over The Crucible PA system as the CPI Forgers football team charges onto the field) and closed at Track 16 by the original October 1986 Progress Street 4-track garage cassette ('Ignition: The Forger's Call [Demo Take 3]', where the band vocalizes 'TING... BOOM!' to test where the foundry anvil strikes), the 16-track compilation chronicles the band's entire Blacksburg collegiate and hometown history—from 1988 campus move-in anthem 'This Side of Heaven' and 1990 acoustic ballad 'Snowfall on Commonwealth Green' to 1992's 'One Dollar on the Kitchen Table', 1998's 'The Old Lady on the Hill' (Bennett Hall), and 2016's brass benediction 'Ad Astra, Per Aspera: Hymn for the Crucible'.

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
